messages:
support_jen: 🚨 ACME reporting spike of 503s starting ~09:12 UTC. They say requests hit hosted endpoint and return 503s intermittently. Customer says it started after a model swap and a traffic jump. Root trace shows upstream container aborts.
eng_oncall_bryan: Looking. Any correlation with deployments or autoscaling events? @ops-bot can you post recent alerts?
ops-bot: ALERT: hosted-infer-upstream-abort count increased from 2 -> 54 in last 10m for pool: hosted-gpu-prod-23; sample reason: ContainerExit(code=137) and Segfault
maria_runtime: I pulled the last three exit logs from the node pool. Two are CUDA OOMs, one is a SIGSEGV in attention kernel. Snippet:
```
2026-03-17T09:13:08Z runner[pid=4123]: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 256 MiB
...
2026-03-17T09:14:02Z runner[pid=4210]: Received SIGSEGV at 0x7f0a2c3d
Backtrace: atn_kernel.cu:237 do_attention()
```
ashwin_ml: This pattern looks like batch fanout growth + kv-prefetch. If a single request suddenly fans out into N contexts during tool calls, it can enlarge active KV and trigger OOM. Did ACME enable tool-calling or provide very long contexts?
support_jen: Customer says they started sending longer system prompts and turned on streaming tool-calls. QPS jumped ~3x. They also mentioned a canary model swap ~09:05 but traffic shifted 09:11.
eng_oncall_bryan: Repro steps we should try locally: emulate ACME payload with long context and toolcall fanout. @ashwin_ml can you share a quick load command?
ashwin_ml: Quick repro (run against staging runner):
```
./loadtest --endpoint https://staging-hosted/v1/gen --concurrency 40 --batch-size 32 \ 
  --context-file acme_long_ctx.json --toolcall-fanout 3 --duration 2m
```
If this causes GPU mem pressure, we have a match.
infra_adam: Also tagging: nodes in that pool had mixed driver versions during the canary rollout. One node reported nvidia-driver v525.60 vs v525.89 on others. Driver mismatch can exacerbate kernel segfaults.
maria_runtime: Good catch. Two of the segfaults happened on nodes with older driver. But the majority are pure OOMs. Short-term mitigation: reduce max_batch_size and disable kv-prefetch at routing layer for that customer route.
eng_oncall_bryan: Can we flip route-level policy to "reduce_batch_and_disable_prefetch" for ACME? Support: can you request permission to apply a temporary config change to their route?
support_jen: ACME approved emergency mitigation, asked for ETA. I'm pushing them a note now.
ops-bot: Config change applied: route/acme/serve_policy => reduce_batch_and_disable_prefetch at 09:23 UTC. Autoscaling unchanged.
eng_oncall_bryan: After flip we should see immediate drop if OOM was the cause. Maria, can you tail pilot metrics? Watch container exit count and 5xx rate.
maria_runtime: Tail: before change 5xx rate 18% on acme-route; after change 09:25 5xx -> 1.6% and container exits dropped from 7/min to 0. Patch reduced OOMs. Still saw one segfault on the older-driver node.
customer_success_lee: ACME reports service back to normal and appreciates quick turnaround. They asked for postmortem and long-term fix.
ashwin_ml: Long-term: we should add a routing knob to enforce per-request KV cap + reject toolcall fanout beyond N for hosted mode or fall back to CPU path for very large contexts. Also add an admission control that rejects massive context growth rather than letting OOMs crash the worker.
eng_oncall_bryan: Agreed. I'll open an incident issue with actionable items. Quick checklist: 1) collect coredumps from segfault node, 2) mark driver mismatch nodes and remediate, 3) add per-route mem guard, 4) add a synthetic test with toolcall fanout in our smoke suite.
ops-bot: Created ticket INF-9876: "ACME upstream aborts on batch fanout -> 503s" assigned eng-runtime; priority P1; link: https://redwood/issue/INF-9876
infra_adam: I'll cordon the old-driver node and schedule a driver bump in the pool. Taking node offline now.
maria_runtime: Collected coredump and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-dumps/INF-9876/coredump-1748889999-4210.txt
eng_oncall_bryan: Temporary mitigation successful, customer impact resolved. Next: schedule 1-hour postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PT. tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml, infra, support.
support_jen: Noted — I'll send calendar invite and the customer-facing summary. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
infra_adam: Postmortem action: add driver homogeneity gating to canary rollout pipeline to avoid mixed-driver pools.
ashwin_ml: Also adding a workload test into preflight that simulates large context + toolcall fanout.
maria_runtime: Closing thread once postmortem created and fix items tracked in INF-9876. Last log: 09:44 UTC no further 503s for ACME.
support_jen: closing loop with customer now. "We've applied a temporary config change to reduce batch sizes and disabled kv-prefetch for your route while we investigate. We'll share a postmortem and roadmap for a permanent fix."
